ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The diagram shows a map with 16 towns which are connected via roads. The government is planning to build power plants in some towns. Each power plant can generate enough electricity for the town in which it stands as well as for its immediate neighbouring towns (i.e. towns that can be reached via a direct connecting road). What is the minimum number of power plants that have to be built?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there are 16 circular towns, arranged in 4 rows and 4 columns. Roads only connect adjacent towns, shown as horizontally adjacent towns in each row being connected and vertically adjacent towns in each column being connected, with no diagonal roads. Therefore the towns can be labeled R1C1 to R4C4. Then reason: one power plant can cover the town where it is located as well as adjacent towns connected by one direct road. From the 4×4 road structure in the figure, it can be seen that one town has at most 4 direct neighbors, so one power plant can cover at most 5 towns. If only 3 power plants are built, they can cover at most 3×5=15 towns, fewer than the 16 towns in the figure, so at least 4 power plants are needed. On the other hand, 4 power plants are sufficient: place them at R1C2, R2C4, R3C1, R4C3. R1C2 covers R1C1, R1C2, R1C3, R2C2; R2C4 covers R1C4, R2C3, R2C4, R3C4; R3C1 covers R2C1, R3C1, R3C2, R4C1; R4C3 covers R3C3, R4C2, R4C3, R4C4. These four groups exactly cover all 16 towns. So the minimum needed is 4 power plants.

For the lower bound, read from the image that no town has more than 4 immediate neighbours, so one plant can cover at most 5 towns total. With only 3 plants, at most 15 towns could be covered, which is fewer than the 16 towns in the diagram, so at least 4 plants are required. For the upper bound, exhibit 4 plant locations, for example R1C2, R2C4, R3C1, and R4C3, and check directly from the grid roads that their closed neighbourhoods cover all 16 towns. Therefore the minimum is 4.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a 4-row, 4-column road grid and label the four corner towns R1C1, R1C4, R4C1, and R4C4. From the text, a plant can cover a town only if it is at graph distance 0 or 1 from that town. For the lower bound, observe from the grid that any two corner towns are at road-distance at least 3 from each other. A single plant cannot cover two such corners, because then the two corners would both be within distance 1 of the plant and hence within distance at most 2 of each other. Thus the four corners require four different plants, so at least 4 plants are needed. For the upper bound, place plants for example at R1C3, R2C1, R3C4, and R4C2; checking their adjacent towns in the image shows they cover every vertex of the 4-by-4 grid. Hence the minimum is 4.
